title: Using finger spaces between words
examples: Why do I need spaces between words?
How big is a finger space?

explain.say: Imagine people standing so close they bump noses. Ouch! Words need a little room too. Look at the board. Which side is easier to read?
Look at the squashed side. All the words are stuck together, like a word traffic jam! It is hard to tell where one word stops and the next one starts. Can you find the word dog?
Now the side with finger spaces. Each word has room to breathe: I, like, my, dog. Much easier! Can you count the words? There are four.
Here is how. Write a word. Then put your pointing finger down right after it. Start the next word on the other side of your finger. Can you try it with your name?

explain.say: Keep going: word, finger, word, finger. Some people use a little stick as a spacer, and that works too. Super spacing! Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this.

faq.a: A finger space is the gap you leave between words. It is about as wide as your finger.

faq.q: How do I make a finger space?
faq.a: Write a word, put your finger on the paper right after it, then start the next word after your finger.
asks: How big is a finger space?

faq.a: Spaces show where one word ends and the next begins. Without them, writing is hard to read, even for you.

faq.q: What if my finger gets in the way?
faq.a: Some writers, often left-handed ones, find their finger gets in the way. You can use a lolly stick, a pencil or just a small gap you can see instead.
asks: I am left-handed and finger spaces are hard

faq.a: A spacer is a little stick, often a lolly stick with a face drawn on it, that you put after each word to make the gap. A teacher or grown-up can help you make one.

facts: English and many other languages leave a space between words when they are written.
Very old writing in Latin and Greek was often written with no spaces between words.

quiz.why: A finger space goes between words, so each word has room.
